question_vi: JavaScript SEO: những lỗi phổ biến khiến Google không index được content?
question_en: JavaScript SEO: what are the common mistakes that prevent Google from indexing content?
answer_vi:
JS SEO có 4 loại lỗi phổ biến khiến Google không index được content — rendering, meta tags, links, và resources.

Lỗi rendering: (1) Content trong useEffect/componentDidMount — Google có thể không chờ async data fetch, (2) Client-only routing (React Router) không có SSR fallback — Google thấy blank page, (3) Error boundaries catch lỗi nhưng render fallback UI — Google index error message thay vì content.

Lỗi meta tags: (4) Dynamic title/description set bằng JS — Google có thể lấy title trước khi JS chạy, (5) Thiếu canonical cho dynamic routes.

Lỗi links: (6) Navigation bằng onClick + router.push thay vì `<a href>` — Google không follow JS click events, (7) Infinite scroll không có pagination fallback.

Lỗi resources: (8) robots.txt block JS/CSS bundles — Google không render được trang, (9) Phụ thuộc long-running JS trước khi render nội dung chính — Google không công bố timeout cố định, nhưng không nên bắt bot chờ JS chạy lâu mới thấy content.

Fix chung: dùng SSR/SSG, test bằng Google Search Console URL Inspection, dùng `<Link>` component cho navigation
answer_en:
JS SEO has 4 common mistake categories that prevent Google from indexing content — rendering, meta tags, links, and resources.

Rendering issues: (1) Content inside useEffect/componentDidMount — Google may not wait for async data fetching, (2) Client-only routing (React Router) without SSR fallback — Google sees a blank page, (3) Error boundaries catching errors and rendering fallback UI — Google indexes the error message instead of real content.

Meta tag issues: (4) Dynamic title/description set via JS — Google may capture the title before JS executes, (5) Missing canonicals for dynamic routes.

Link issues: (6) Navigation using onClick + router.push instead of `<a href>` — Google does not follow JS click events, (7) Infinite scroll without a pagination fallback.

Resource issues: (8) robots.txt blocking JS/CSS bundles — Google cannot render the page, (9) Depending on long-running JS before the main content renders — Google has no published fixed rendering timeout, but bots should not have to wait on slow JS to see content.

General fixes: use SSR/SSG, test with Google Search Console URL Inspection, use a `<Link>` component for all navigation
